{{Quote|They hoped to fill me with fear. But fear leads to anger. Anger leads to hate. And hate…leads to power.|Darth Vader|<ref name="Darth Vader (2020) 10">[[Darth Vader (2020) 10|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 10]]</ref>}}
The '''Sith''', also referred to as the '''Sith Order''', was an ancient [[Religion|religious]] order of [[Force-sensitive|Force-wielders]] devoted to the [[dark side of the Force]]. Driven by their raw emotions, including hate, anger, and greed, the Sith were deceptive and obsessed with gaining power no matter the cost. The order had many forms until it reached the apex of its power under [[Darth Sidious]], the [[Dark Lord of the Sith]] who achieved his order's goal of [[Galaxy|galactic]] conquest after a [[millennium]] of [[Grand Plan|plotting]]. Within a generation, however, the [[death]]s of Darth Sidious and [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] marked the end of the [[Sith Lord]]s. Though the Sith ultimately went extinct with Sidious's demise, they still had a powerful legacy, and many continued to follow their teachings. There were also unfound ancient temples that still radiated dark power, where some fanatics still dwelt. 

Thousands of [[Standard year|years]] before the [[Clone Wars]], the [[Jedi Order]] was fractured by a [[Hundred-Year Darkness|schism]] that began when a [[Unidentified rogue Jedi|rogue Jedi]] and his [[Jedi splinter group|followers]] turned away from the [[light side of the Force]], believing the dark side was the path to true power. Having relocated to the [[planet]] [[Moraband|Korriban]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories]], their movement ultimately evolved into the Sith Order, resulting in a [[Sith war (Old Republic)|war]] between the former brothers and sisters in [[the Force]] as the [[Jedi Knight]]s rallied to the defense of the [[Galactic Republic|Old Republic]]. Although the Sith were driven off of the [[Core Worlds|Core World]] [[Coruscant]] by [[5000 BBY]], [[Standard century|centuries]] of conflict ensued between the two orders, culminating in the Old Republic's [[Fall of the Old Republic|collapse]]. Undermined by constant infighting and ruined by the [[Jedi-Sith War|last war]] against the [[Jedi]], the Sith were rendered all but extinct with the exception of one; [[Darth Bane]] survived the ancient order's destruction and passed his knowledge to a single apprentice, [[Darth Zannah]], before being entombed on Korriban, which became known as Moraband. Henceforth, the Sith was governed by the [[Rule of Two]], a new philosophy dictating that only two Sith [[Lord]]s—a [[Sith Master]] and a [[Sith apprentice]]—could exist at any given [[time]]. As a result, the Sith were all but forgotten while the Jedi focused their efforts on [[Law enforcement agency|preserving]] the [[Republic Era|new age of peace]] under the modern Galactic Republic.

The Sith remained in hiding for a millennium until the rise of [[Darth]] Sidious and [[Maul|Darth Maul]] in [[32 BBY]]. Sidious, trained by [[Darth Plagueis]], hid in plain sight as [[Senator]] Sheev Palpatine of [[Naboo]]. Orchestrating the [[blockade]] and [[Invasion of Naboo|invasion]] of his [[homeworld]] by the [[Trade Federation]], Sidious maneuvered the [[Galactic Senate]] into electing him to the [[Office of the Chancellor|office]] of [[Supreme Chancellor]]. His entire chancellery would encompass the [[Republic Era|final years]] of the Republic. Over the next [[Standard decade|decade]] Sidious sowed the seeds of discontent within the galactic populace with the help of his new apprentice, the former [[Jedi Master]] [[Count]] [[Dooku]], who adopted the name of Darth Tyranus and became the public face of the [[Independent Movement for Self-Determination]]. The [[Separatist Crisis]] culminated in the formation of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]] and the creation of the [[Separatist Droid Army]] which, in turn, compelled the Senate to support the establishment of the [[Grand Army of the Republic]]. [[Jar Jar Binks]], acting in place of Senator [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Amidala]], started a motion to grant the [[Supreme Chancellor]] emergency powers.

The [[Cloning|Clone]] Wars began with the [[First Battle of Geonosis]] in [[22 BBY]], after which entire [[Army|armies]] of [[battle droid]]s and [[clone trooper]]s deployed across [[the galaxy]], making war and devastation commonplace for the first time since the [[1032 BBY|formation of the Republic]]. In the final [[Standard month|months]] of the Clone Wars, Sidious [[Battle of Coruscant|sacrificed]] and betrayed Tyranus as part of his plot to turn Anakin Skywalker, the Jedi Order's prophesied [[Chosen One]], to the dark side. Playing on Skywalker's fear of losing his secret [[Marriage|wife]], Senator [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]], Palpatine revealed his deception and true identity, while claiming that the dark side was the path to [[immortality]]. Members of the [[Jedi High Council]], having learned from Skywalker's report that the chancellor was, in fact, a Sith Lord, attempted to [[Prison|arrest]] Palpatine, but the chancellor resisted. Torn between his faith in the Jedi and the fate he foresaw for his wife, Skywalker ultimately chose the Sith by betraying [[Mace Windu]], allowing Sidious to kill the Jedi Order's great champion.

Using the [[Duel in Palpatine's office|incident]] in the [[Emperor's office|chancellor's office]] to frame the Jedi Order for [[treason]], Sidious declared [[Order 66]] was in effect, marking all Jedi as enemies of the state and susceptible to execution. The clone [[trooper]]s' [[Behavioral modification biochip|programming]] turned them against their [[Jedi General]]s, who were betrayed and [[Death penalty|executed]] across the galaxy. With the majority of the order falling victim to the [[Great Jedi Purge]], Sidious [[Proclamation of the New Order|announced]] the creation of a [[New Order|new regime]], transforming the Republic into the [[Galactic Empire|First Galactic Empire]] in [[19 BBY]]. With the former Anakin Skywalker, renamed Darth Vader, at his side, the self-proclaimed [[Galactic Emperor]]'s rise to power was complete, and the Sith were restored to dominance after centuries of plotting.

The Sith's control of the galaxy remained relatively unchallenged for a [[Imperial Era|generation]] until the [[Declaration of Rebellion|birth]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] which, in turn, led to the [[Galactic Civil War]] in [[1 BBY]]. The Emperor, having felt a [[disturbance in the Force]], discovered that his apprentice's long lost [[Skywalker family|son]], [[Luke Skywalker]], was [[Jedi training|training]] to become a Jedi. Aware of the potential Luke inherited from his [[Parent|father]], the Emperor foresaw the possibility of his own destruction but resolved to turn the young man to the dark side as he did with Vader. During the [[Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY]], the Emperor forced father and son into a [[Lightsaber duel|duel]], which ended with Luke disarming Vader. The Emperor subsequently betrayed Vader by ordering Luke to finish him off and be Sidious's apprentice, but the young Jedi Knight refused. Knowing he had lost Luke to the Jedi, the Emperor proceeded to [[torture]] Luke with torrents of [[Force lightning]]. At that moment, Vader, overwhelmed by his son's compassion for him, chose to save Luke by killing his master. 

The death of the now redeemed Anakin Skywalker, marked the extinction of the Sith, who then succumbed to his injuries—bringing balance to the Force. Yet while the ancient [[Chosen One]] prophecy foretold the Sith's demise, it never predicted the end of the dark side. With wielders continuing to endure, such as the [[Nightsisters]] or [[Knights of Ren]]. After the [[First Order]] [[Cold War|rise]] from the [[Unknown Regions]], the enigmatic darksider [[Supreme Leader]] [[Snoke]] [[throne]] was [[Battle of Oetchi|succeeded]] by [[Ben Solo|Kylo Ren]]—nephew of [[Jedi Master]] Skywalker during the [[First Order-Resistance War|war]] against the [[Resistance]]. Snoke was in fact only a [[Strand-Cast|creation and tool]] of a reborn Darth Sidious after he [[Palpatine's broadcast|announced]] his return to the galaxy and revealed the [[Final Order]]. The clone emperor and his cults—the [[Sith Eternal]] emergence from hiding resulted in a desperate final [[Battle of Exegol|battle]] against the him which saw the Jedi [[Rey Skywalker|Rey]] and a redeemed Ben Solo to destroy Sidious, permanently preventing the rebirth of the Sith.

==Philosophy==
===The Code of the Sith===
{{Quote|Anger and pain are natural and part of growth. They give you focus. They make you strong.|Darth Vader|<ref name="Backstories Vader" />}}
[[File:DarthVader22.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Generations of Sith adhered to a philosophy of power through the dark side of the Force.]]
The Sith focused on primal emotions like anger and pain in order to gain power from the [[dark side of the Force]]. The [[Code of the Sith]] was the antithesis of the [[Jedi Code]], although like its counterpart, it governed the actions and beliefs of the Sith. The Sith code insisted on the importance of passion and the rejection of peace.<ref name="Backstories Vader" />

:''Peace is a lie. There is only passion.''
:''Through passion I gain strength.''
:''Through strength I gain power.''
:''Through power I gain victory.''
:''Through victory my chains are broken.''
:''The Force shall free me.''<ref name="Secrets of the Sith" />

The Sith wore [[clothing]] that obscured their identity while in hiding.<ref name="VE" /> They used the term "dark side" because they were secretive. The Sith felt it was easier to impose order if they kept their identities and knowledge a secret or, as [[Lona Aphra]] put it, "hidden—in the dark."<ref name="Aphra 32">[[Doctor Aphra (2016) 32|''Doctor Aphra'' (2016) 32]]</ref> The [[Sith Eternal crest|hex charm]] was a traditional symbol of the Sith.<ref name="Shadow of the Sith" /> [[Jedi Master]] [[Zallah Macri]] maintained that, in the abstract, the Sith Order's ideals may have seemed "good" to a Jedi, but the finer details and their actions painted a clearer picture for what they truly stood for.<ref name="POD">''[[The High Republic: Path of Deceit]]''</ref> Indeed, many who joined the Sith<ref name="Episode III" /> or related dark side groups tried to rationalize their actions at first<ref name="The Fallen Star">''[[The High Republic: The Fallen Star]]''</ref> before being fully consumed by the dark side.<ref name="Episode III" />

===The Doctrine of the Dyad===
{{Quote|The Doctrine of the Dyad was etched into the walls of my citadel on Exegol eons ago, a constant reminder of its significance to our Order. To my Sith Eternal, the dyad is not merely the stuff of ancient legend; it is the future of the Sith—the key to unlocking the full potential of the dark side.|Darth Sidious|<ref name="Secrets of the Sith" />}}
[[File:Dyad.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The Doctrine of the Dyad preceded the Sith Order's Rule of Two.]]
The [[Doctrine of the Dyad]] arose from the concept of a [[Force dyad]]. A dyad was a powerful [[Force-bond]] connecting two [[Force-sensitive]]s; the bond transcended their physical beings and combined them into one presence in [[the Force]]. The beings in a dyad possessed rare abilities that were unique to their bond, and therefore unattainable to those who lacked a dyadic connection, regardless of their own strength or experience with the Force. Over the generations, the Sith sought in vain to create a dyad through sheer willpower, believing it was the key to achieving the ultimate power of the dark side. The [[Sith Lord]] [[Darth Sidious]] viewed the dyad as a source of limitless power.<ref name="Secrets of the Sith" />

The Doctrine of the Dyad was etched into the walls of the [[Sith Citadel]] on [[Exegol]], eons before Sidious' time, to remind the Sith of the dyad's significance to their Order.<ref name="Secrets of the Sith" /> The Doctrine of the Dyad also influenced the [[Sith Eternal]], a [[Sith cult|cult]] of [[Sith cultist|Sith devotees]] who [[Doctrine of the Dyad|predicted]] the return of the dyad.<ref name="TROS VD" /> Like the Sith Order, the Sith Eternal believed that the dyad was essential to realizing the dark side's full potential.<ref name="Secrets of the Sith" />

===The Rule of Two===
{{Quote|But there was a Sith Lord who survived the culling—the great Darth Bane. It was he who reshaped the Sith, creating a new hierarchy to ensure the survival of our Order. His Rule of Two dictated that only two Sith Lords could exist at any one time—a master to possess the unlimited power of the dark side and an apprentice to covet it.|Darth Sidious|<ref name="Secrets of the Sith" />}}
[[File:SithOrder-SOTJ.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Rule of Two governed the Sith Order for a millennium, from its ancient founder to the last Dark Lord of the Sith.]]
Even before the formation of the [[Rule of Two]] that decreed only two Sith—a [[Sith Master]] and a [[Sith apprentice]]—could exist at one time,<ref name="Secrets of the Sith" /> the Sith of old often found themselves ruled by two Sith in specific, who would reign over their many fellow Sith.<ref name="TROS JN">''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: A Junior Novel]]''</ref> The Rule of Two, however, would officially limit the Sith Order's numbers due to the infighting that had ruined it. The rule nonetheless ensured the relationship between a Sith Master and their apprentice was not one of trust; indeed, both the master and the apprentice constantly searched for any sign of weakness in the other, for a weak master deserved to be overthrown by their pupil, just as a weak pupil deserved to be replaced by a worthier, more powerful recruit. This philosophy was embraced by the Sith, who adopted it as a way to purify the weak and become stronger over time, since only an apprentice who had surpassed all previous Sith could take their master's place through honorable combat.<ref name="Backstories Vader" />

The Sith were free to train dark side agents identified as [[Sith acolyte]]s<ref name="Dark Disciple">''[[Dark Disciple]]''</ref> so long as those acolytes were not trained as true Sith Lords. However, it was more than possible the Sith apprentice would violate the Rule of Two by training an acolyte as a real apprentice, intending to have their aid in overthrowing the Sith Master.<ref name="Nightsisters">{{TCW|Nightsisters (episode)}}</ref> The concept of the dyad influenced the philosophy of the Rule of Two, emphasized the power of two Force-sensitives working in tandem to grow even more powerful as an Order. As the successor of the Doctrine of the Dyad, the Rule of Two was seen as a "pale imitation" of its predecessor by Darth Sidious.<ref name="Secrets of the Sith" />

==History==
===Ancient times===
====The Hundred-Year Darkness====
{{Quote|Once we were brothers in the Force. But from the Hundred-Year Darkness were born the Sith.|Unidentified Jedi|<ref name="SW9" />}}
[[File:Moraband_Planet.png|thumb|left|180px|Korriban, later known as Moraband, was settled by the Sith following their schism with the Jedi Order.]]
Formed around [[5000 BBY]]<ref name="Timelines" />, the Sith were the ancient enemies of the [[Jedi Order]]<ref name="SW9">[[Star Wars (2015) 9|''Star Wars'' (2015) 9]]</ref> who shared their name with a [[Sith (species)|red-skinned species]].<ref name="3rd Grade and Writing">''[[Star Wars Workbook: 3rd Grade Reading and Writing]]''</ref> Established by a [[Unidentified rogue Jedi|rogue Jedi]] during the [[Hundred-Year Darkness]], the Sith sought further knowledge and power through learning the dark side of the Force. Eventually, this [[Jedi]] was able to amass a [[Jedi splinter group]] with a sizable following, all of whom adhered to this new philosophy that embraced the dark side.<ref name="Sith" /> This schism in the Jedi Order led to a civil war where the Jedi and the newly-founded Sith Order, once brothers and sisters in the Force, fought against one another for power.<ref name="SW9" /> The war ended in the defeat of the Sith, who fled from known [[Realspace|space]]. Unbeknownst to the Jedi, however, the Sith settled on [[Moraband|Korriban]], a [[Planet|world]] of [[Color|red]] sands that was later known as Moraband, where they rebuilt in secret and waited for another chance to strike.<ref name="Sith" />

====Exile on Korriban====
{{Quote|Known long ago as Korriban, this ancient homeworld of the Sith was abandoned after countless wars transformed it into an infertile wasteland.|Darth Sidious|<ref name="Secrets of the Sith" />}}
[[File:Valley_of_the_Dark_Lords_TCW.png|thumb|right|250px|Sith temples and monuments were constructed on Korriban during the time of the ancient Sith.]]
As the Sith Order grew, they constructed massive [[Sith temple|temples]] and tombs on Korriban in a location known as the [[Valley of the Dark Lords]].<ref name="Sacrifice" /> The Sith built [[Sith Empire|empires]] on the backs of their [[Slavery|slaves]]<ref name="EfK" /> and fought wars against the Jedi for control of the galaxy. During these wars, they built massive [[superweapon]]s powered by giant [[kyber crystal]]s.<ref name="The Big Bang">{{TCW|The Big Bang}}</ref><ref name="Death Star Superlaser">{{Databank|death-star-superlaser|Death Star Superlaser}}</ref> Eventually, a trade route in the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] came to be known as the [[Cloak of the Sith]], a name which<ref name="Smuggler's Guide">''[[Star Wars: Smuggler's Guide]]''</ref> was similar to how Sith Lords were known to wear dark cloaks.<ref name="Episode VI" />

====War on the Old Republic====
{{Quote|The Sith Order grew, spreading its might across the galaxy.|Darth Sidious|<ref name="Secrets of the Sith" />}}
[[File:TrappedDrengir-2021THR4.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The Sith encountered and later betrayed the Drengir.]]
It was believed the [[lightfoil]] was made by the early Sith.<ref name="Knights of Fate">''[[Knights of Fate]]''</ref> The Sith also formed an alliance with the [[Nightsisters]] of [[Dathomir]] at some point, but the "old alliance," as they came to dub it, eventually ceased. Ultimately, the Nightsisters would decide to only retain loyalty to each other.<ref name="Monster">{{TCW|Monster}}</ref> Around [[2500 BBY]], the Sith allied with the [[Drengir]], and for a [[time]] they worked alongside each other, until around the same year<ref name="Timelines" /> they betrayed the living plants.<ref name="The High Republic (2021) 4">[[The High Republic (2021) 4|''The High Republic'' (2021) 4]]</ref> The Sith [[Capture of the Drengir|left the Drengir]] locked on the [[Amaxine Space Station|Amaxine space station]] via the [[binding statues]].<ref name="ItD">''[[The High Republic: Into the Dark]]''</ref> 

[[Exim Panshard]] was a Sith [[viceroy]] who ruled over a [[Unidentified planet (Exim Panshard)|forgotten planet]] in a bloody rule, culminating in the creation of a [[Mask of Viceroy Exim Panshard|mask]] that, fueled by the deaths of countless civilians, he cling onto life within.<ref name="Shadow of the Sith" />

[[File:GreatSithWarsBas-Relief-SW100Objects.png|thumb|right|300px|The Jedi and Sith waged a series of wars throughout their history so ruinous that at points each was brought to the brink of destruction.]]
At one point, nearly five thousand [[Standard year|years]] before the [[Proclamation of the New Order|rise]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], the Sith waged a [[Sith war (Old Republic)|war]] against the Jedi and the Old Republic. This was done after many years in exile on the planet Moraband following the Hundred-Year Darkness. During this war, the Sith [[Battle of Coruscant (Sith war)|attacked]] the Republic capital [[Coruscant]].<ref name="CL2016" /> This allowed the Sith to build a [[Shrine in the Depths|shrine]] on the planet, which became a place of immense dark side power. Eventually, the Jedi were able to repel the Sith from Coruscant. The Jedi raised their own [[Imperial Palace|temple]] over the Coruscant shrine in an attempt to contain and eliminate its power.<ref name="Tarkin" />

Around this time, the Jedi and Sith engaged in a number of battles and wars like the [[Great Hyperspace War]]<ref name="Nexus" /> and the [[Great Sith Wars]].<ref name="sw100">''[[Star Wars 100 Objects]]''</ref> The [[Massassi]], a [[Slavery|slave]] [[Species|race]] controlled by the Sith, constructed the [[Great Temple]] on [[Yavin 4]], allegedly under the leadership of the Sith [[Lord]] [[Naga Sadow]].<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars">''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]''</ref><ref name="BTM">{{BuildFalconCite|23|Guide to the Galaxy}}</ref>

====A bastion of the Sith====
{{Quote|It was here on… on this dead world… that the Jedi struck a terrible blow against the Sith. Many of our order were struck down. All because they wanted to be ''free''.|Darth Sidious, to Darth Maul|<ref name="Darth Maul (2017) 2">[[Darth Maul (2017) 2|''Darth Maul'' (2017) 2]]</ref>}}
[[File:GreatScourgeofMalachor-TotA1.png|thumb|left|250px|Jedi and Sith both perished when Malachor was scourged by the power within an ancient Sith temple.]]
The Sith continued to expand their empire erecting temples on multiple planets. One such [[Malachor Sith Temple|temple]] was built on the world [[Malachor]]. At the heart of this temple was a [[Malachor superweapon|superweapon]] powered by a giant kyber crystal. The Jedi eventually learned of the weapon and assaulted the temple. A savage [[Great Scourge of Malachor|battle]] was then waged between the Sith Empire and the invading Jedi Knights. During the battle, the temple was activated, petrifying everyone on the planet. This would result in the planet being forbidden from Jedi and becoming a legend for millennia to come.<ref name="Twilight" />

====Resurgence of the Sith====
Over the course of thousands of years, the rivalry between the Sith and Jedi took many forms.<ref name="Insider230">{{InsiderCite|230|Launchpad}}</ref> The Sith [[Resurgence of the Sith|resurged]] in one conflict that became very desperate, which was likely why the Jedi Order turned to [[Form VII]] "Juyo." That aggressive lightsaber combat form, however, resulted in a number of Jedi falling to the dark side. After the conflict had finished, the Jedi banned its study.<ref name="Knights of Fate" />

====The rise and fall of Darth Momin====
{{Quote|With resources inherited from Lady Shaa and the help of acolytes desperate to aid me in my work, I designed a great engine. It was a weapon, of course, powerful enough to burn the city to ash.|Darth Momin, to Darth Vader|<ref name="Dark Lord of the Sith 22" />}}
[[File:MominActivatesWeapon-2017DarthVader22.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Darth Momin venerated the power of the dark side of the Force.]]
The Sith Lord [[Darth Momin]], after killing his Master [[Darth Shaa]], sought more knowledge in the dark side. He decided that his only audience was the Force and yearned to be worthy of it. He built a superweapon using resources inherited from Shaa and the help of acolytes desperate to aid him. [[Darth Momin's superweapon]] had the power to incinerate an entire city, but his true plan was different. He wanted to pour the Force into the weapon's engine and freeze the terrified expressions of the people in time forever, creating an artwork depicting fear and pain devoted to the dark side of the Force. When he [[Darth Momin's destruction of a city|attempted]] this, the Jedi intervened and Momin's body was destroyed, yet his mind remained inside his [[Mask of Lord Momin|mask]] where he waited for his revival as ages passed.<ref name="Dark Lord of the Sith 22" />

In the meantime, however, the Sith buried knowledge of Momin and his ideas on the belief that he had been a heretic. The Sith refused to recount information about Momin into their holocrons. The Jedi, too, made no mention of the Sith Lord in their holocrons<ref name="Dark Lord 21">[[Darth Vader (2017) 21|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 21]]</ref> and locked his mask away.<ref name="Dark Lord 8">[[Darth Vader (2017) 8|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 8]]</ref> Nonetheless, the Sith at some point used<ref name="Dark Droids 1">[[Dark Droids 1|''Dark Droids'' 1]]</ref> Momin's [[Fermata Cage]]<ref name="HE 2">[[Hidden Empire 2|''Hidden Empire'' 2]]</ref> to lock away a [[Unidentified droid (Fermata Cage)|droid intelligence]].<ref name="Dark Droids 1" /> The Fermata Cage was then hidden within a [[dark side hellscape]]<ref name="Crimson Reign 5">[[Crimson Reign 5|''Crimson Reign'' 5]]</ref> Momin knew of.<ref name="Dark Lord of the Sith 22" />

====The Dark Age====
{{Quote|After thousands of years of war, the Sith were pushed to the edge of extinction.|Darth Sidious|<ref name="Secrets of the Sith" />}}
During a period of time known as the [[Fall of the Old Republic|Dark Age]], the [[Jedi-Sith War]] broke out. Early on in the war, the Sith [[Battle of Coruscant (Jedi-Sith War)|attacked]] the Old Republic capital world of Coruscant. The Sith successfully captured the planet as well as the Jedi Temple. The [[Liberation of Coruscant]] was one of the last battles of the Jedi-Sith War and resulted in the Sith being driven from Coruscant.<ref name="SWP">''[[Star Wars Propaganda: A History of Persuasive Art in the Galaxy]]''</ref>

====Destruction and rebirth====
{{Quote|A long, long time ago, there were many Sith. We rose up against the simpering light…we warred with the Jedi…and lost as we also warred amongst our own kind.|Darth Sidious, to Darth Vader|<ref name="Darth Vader 20">[[Darth Vader (2015) 20|''Darth Vader'' (2015) 20]]</ref>}}
[[File:DarthBane-2020DarthVader27variant.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The Sith were reformed by Darth Bane, who decreed that only two Sith Lords could exist at any given time: a master and an apprentice.]]
The Sith numbered thousands, yet they were eventually<ref name="Fun Facts">{{SWKidsYouTube|series=Star Wars Galaxy of Adventures Fun Facts|text=The Sith|video=wQ0GhIIgQAk}}</ref> [[Defeat of the Sith|defeated]] at<ref name="Helmet Collection 29">{{HelmetCollectionCite|29|Databank A-Z}}</ref> the world<ref name="VE" /> of [[Ruusan]]<ref name="Helmet Collection 29" /> in the [[Mid Rim Territories]].<ref name="VE" /> Despite the [[Sith armada]]'s quantitative advantage over the much smaller [[Ghostfinder fleet]], the Sith were outmatched.<ref name="EE" /> The Sith's quest to gain power was ultimately their undoing, as the dark side made them turn against one another. Within a year, the Jedi managed to defeat the infighting Sith, bringing what was left of the dark order to its knees. However, one Sith, [[Darth Bane]], survived. With his fellow Sith Lords destroyed, he reformed the order by establishing the Rule of Two, mandating that only two Sith, a master and an apprentice, could exist at any given time, lest they fall prey to infighting.<ref name="Sacrifice" /> To keep Bane's philosophy alive, the apprentice needed to slay their master and take on an apprentice of their own, or the master could train another apprentice and have them kill and replace their current apprentice. Bane had also initiated a revenge plot against the Jedi, called the [[Grand Plan]].<ref name="Episode III" />

The Sith abandoned their traditional [[homeworld]] of Moraband after it was scarred by many wars.<ref name="datamora">{{Databank|moraband|Moraband}}</ref> Eventually, [[Darth]] Bane was [[Death|killed]] and was [[Tomb of Darth Bane|buried]] in the Valley of the Dark Lords on its surface,<ref name="Sacrifice" /> but the Rule of Two continued through his apprentice, [[Darth Zannah]]. It was rumored that Zannah had killed Bane on the [[Inner Rim Territories|Inner Rim]] [[planet]] of [[Ambria]].<ref name="HC 2">{{HelmetCollectionCite|2|Databank A-Z}}</ref> The Jedi believed that they had destroyed Bane's rule and,<ref name="SW 2020 20">[[Star Wars (2020) 20|''Star Wars'' (2020) 20]]</ref> incorrectly thinking the Sith extinct,<ref name="Episode I" /> entered into a golden age<ref name="SW 2020 20" /> remembered as the [[High Republic Era]].<ref name="Kylo 2">[[The Rise of Kylo Ren 2|''The Rise of Kylo Ren'' 2]]</ref> Many Sith worlds were also quarantined, including [[Rhelg]], [[Jaguada]], and [[Ziost]]. Some worlds were so cleansed of their Sith history that even locals had no idea of their past.<ref name="TROS VD" /> The [[Lerct Historical Institute]] forbade research into the Sith as something arcane and occult that had no place among its work.<ref name="Shadow of the Sith" />

===In the shadows===
====High Republic Era====
=====Threat of the Nameless=====
{{Quote|This act was a ''gift'', to everyone who touches the Force. Jedi, Sith, ''all of us''.|Azlin Rell, to Yoda|<ref name="SOS 1">[[The High Republic – Shadows of Starlight 1|''The High Republic – Shadows of Starlight'' 1]]</ref>}}
[[File:AllOfUs-THRSOS1.png|thumb|left|250px|The fallen Jedi Azlin Rell invoked the name of the Sith when justifying the destruction of an entire city on Travyx Prime as a gift to all Force-sensitives.]]
The Sith stayed in hiding for a thousand years, their survival unknown to the Jedi, as they continued their revenge against the Jedi through Bane's Grand Plan. With Sith teachings passed down by Bane's Rule of Two, the Order managed to survive.<ref name="Sacrifice" /> During the High Republic Era, the [[Shrikarai|Nameless]] beings emerged as a major threat to any individual sensitive to the Force. Former Jedi [[Azlin Rell]]—who fell to the dark side out of his fear and lost his mind—resolved to wipe out the entire species, reasoning that such would be a gift to every Force-sensitive in the galaxy, including the Sith. While he made it clear to the Jedi High Council that he was not their enemy because he was no Sith, Rell ensured a [[Unidentified Travyx Prime city|city]] on the world [[Travyx Prime]] was [[Attack on Travyx Prime|destroyed]], thereby silencing a possible lead to the Nameless homeworld, [[Sophros|Planet X]]. He proclaimed to Yoda his actions were a gift to every Force user, including the Jedi and Sith,<ref name="SOS 1" /> but Yoda did not take his words as proof of the Sith Order's return.<ref name="Episode I" />

=====The Stranger=====
======Masters of shadows======
{{Quote|What are you?''"<br />"''I have no name. But the Jedi like you might call me… Sith.|Sol and the Stranger|<ref name="Night">{{Acolyte|Night}}</ref>}}
[[File:TheStrangerPushes-Day.png|thumb|right|250px|The Stranger, also known as "the Master," was a mysterious Sith who sought to train an acolyte.]]
By the later period of the High Republic Era,<ref name="The Acolyte">{{Acolyte|The Acolyte (episode)}}</ref> a [[Dark Lord of the Sith]] named [[Darth Plagueis]]<ref name="Episode III" /> was active.<ref name="The Acolyte" /> Furthermore, a [[The Stranger|human Jedi]]<ref name="Teach / Corrupt">{{Acolyte|Teach / Corrupt}}</ref> trained by Jedi Master [[Vernestra Rwoh]]<ref name="The Acolyte" /> fell to the dark side of the Force<ref name="Night">{{Acolyte|Night}}</ref> and abandoned the Jedi Order, keeping himself out of Rwoh's reach.<ref name="The Acolyte" /> The individual, who claimed to have no name<ref name="Night">{{Acolyte|Night}}</ref> and thus became known as "the Stranger,"<ref name="Qimir DB">{{Databank|qimir|The Stranger (alias "Qimir")}}</ref> became a Sith<ref name="Stunts">{{SWYouTube|4RGDVX3pBgs|The Acolyte | Lightsaber Stunts | Disney+}}</ref> as the apprentice to Plagueis.<ref name="Leslye EW">{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/the-acolyte-creator-leslye-headland-season-2-heard-nothing-8681155|text=''The Acolyte'' creator says she has heard nothing about getting a potential season 2|author=Ross, Dalton|date=2024-07-26|archivedate=20250318052542}}</ref>

The Stranger also operated<ref name="Night" /> publicly as the [[merchant]]<ref name="Revenge Justice">{{Acolyte|Revenge / Justice}}</ref> Qimir.<ref name="Night" /> The Stranger kept his identity well-hidden<ref name="Revenge Justice">{{Acolyte|Revenge / Justice}}</ref> and sought to see the dream of the Jedi Order overthrown.<ref name="Lost / Found">{{Acolyte|Lost / Found}}</ref> It was his ultimate hope to wield his power however he wished.<ref name="Night" /> A location also known to Plagueis,<ref name="The Acolyte" /> he based himself within an [[The Stranger's island|island]] [[the Stranger's cave|cave]] located on<ref name="Cave Stranger">{{Databank|the-stranger-s-cave|The Stranger's Cave}}</ref> the planet<ref name="AcolyteVG">''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte: The Visual Guide]]''</ref> [[Bal'demnic]],<ref name="Fry">{{EmailCite|email=File:AtlasEmail-2025-10-24.png|creator=[[Jason Fry]]|date=2025-10-24}}</ref> where he could operate without the knowledge of the Jedi.<ref name="Cave Stranger" /> Plagueis took to lurking<ref name="Acolyte Companion">{{InsiderCite|229|Star Wars: The Acolyte Companion|''Star Wars: The Acolyte'' Companion}}</ref> in the shadows around the Stranger's dwelling. Combined with the Stranger's reluctance to call himself a Sith, the dark side user's true loyalties thus remained elusive, especially as they related to Plagueis.<ref name="229POV">{{InsiderCite|229|A Certain Point of View (department)}}</ref>

======Searching for an acolyte======
{{Quote|What do you want?''"<br />"''Freedom. The freedom to wield my power the way I like. Without having to answer to Jedi like you. I want a pupil, an Acolyte.|Sol and the Stranger|<ref name="Night" />}}
[[File:RevengeJusticeThumbnailAcolyte.png|thumb|left|250px|Mae-ho Aniseya was trained as an acolyte and Sith assassin by the Stranger.]]
In time, the Stranger sought out a disciple to train<ref name="Night" /> despite the Rule of Two:<ref name="Sacrifice" /> his decision was to train a Sith acolyte,<ref name="Night" /> a position that, in theory, would exist outside the rule.<ref name="Nightsisters" /> He eventually discovered a human woman named [[Mae-ho Aniseya]], who in childhood had been part of a [[Brendok coven|witch coven]] alongside her twin sister [[Verosha Aniseya]] until an [[Mission to Brendok|incident involving the Jedi Order]]<ref name="Destiny Acolyte">{{Acolyte|Destiny (The Acolyte)}}</ref> in [[148 BBY]].<ref name="148 Date">{{TheAcolyteDate}} "[[Destiny (The Acolyte)|Destiny]]" dates itself to sixteen [[Standard year|years]] before the series' main events, equating to [[148 BBY]].</ref> With the Sith keeping his identity a secret,<ref name="Night" /> Mae swore herself to and began to be trained by the individual, whom she knew only as "the Master,"<ref name="Revenge Justice">{{Acolyte|Revenge / Justice}}</ref> out of a desire to have revenge on the [[Brendok four|four Jedi involved in the Brendok mission]], among them Jedi Master [[Sol]], who had slain her mother [[Aniseya]]<ref name="The Acolyte" /> out of a misunderstanding and then covered up his actions.<ref name="Choice">{{Acolyte|Choice}}</ref> Ultimately, Mae sought to please "the Master"<ref name="Revenge Justice">{{Acolyte|Revenge / Justice}}</ref> but feared the man as well.<ref name="Day">{{Acolyte|Day (episode)}}</ref> Under his public cover,<ref name="Night" /> "Qimir" worked with Mae as a trader of rare goods<ref name="Revenge Justice" /> and fellow servant of the Master,<ref name="Day">{{Acolyte|Day (episode)}}</ref> with Mae unaware he was none-other-than her mentor.<ref name="Night" /> The Master further, in the words of his Qimir persona, "collected" people, which was "Qimir's" cover story.<ref name="Day" />

[[File:QimirLightsabers-Night.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Stranger killed several Jedi in order to ensure that his identity as a Sith remained concealed.]]
Under the Master's tutelage,<ref name="Revenge Justice" /> Mae served as a [[Sith assassin]]<ref name="114 Interview">{{GermanFanCite|114|Star Wars: The Acolyte: There Are Always Four – No More, No Less…|''Star Wars: The Acolyte'': There Are Always Four – No More, No Less…}}</ref> and acolyte.<ref name="Night" /> Eventually, he demanded she slay a Jedi without a weapon as her final test. As per his wishes, Mae began a [[Mae's quest|quest]] to kill the four Jedi involved in her past, Masters Sol, [[Torbin]], [[Indara]], and [[Kelnacca]],<ref name="Revenge Justice" /> in [[132 BBY]].<ref name="148 Date" /> After the deaths of Indara and Torbin, with the former killed at her own hand with a knife but the latter having taken his own life when confronted by Mae, Mae learned that her sister was in fact alive,<ref name="Revenge Justice" /> which ultimately convinced her to abandon her life as the Master's servant during her [[Mission to Khofar|mission to slay Kelnacca]]. Unknown to Mae, the Master himself had arrived<ref name="Day" />—as he was none-other-than Qimir,<ref name="Night" /> who she betrayed and left "trapped" in the woods—and would kill Kelnacca himself. Afterward, he engaged a grouping of Jedi under Sol who had journeyed to [[Kelnacca's shelter]],<ref name="Day" /> slaughtering all but Sol over the course of the battle. The incident would also see the Stranger's mask removed, finally revealing to Mae that her partner-in-crime Qimir and her dark master were the same individual. The Stranger further revealed himself as a Sith to Sol.<ref name="Night" />

======Stranger no more======
{{Quote|I need you to help me find someone.''"<br />"''Who?''"<br />"''A pupil of mine before he turned to evil.|Vernestra Rwoh and Mae-ho Aniseya|<ref name="The Acolyte" />}}
[[File:QimirPointIsland-TeachCorrupt.png|thumb|left|250px|Mae-ho Aniseya had fallen out with the Stranger, who directed his attention to her twin sister, Verosha Aniseya.]]
After Qimir's double identity was revealed and the Sith was swarmed by a grouping of [[umbramoth]]s, Mae knocked out her sister and swapped places with her, returning to the Jedi transport with Sol. Meanwhile, the Stranger reclaimed his mask and cloak before finding the unconscious Osha,<ref name="Night" /> who he brought back with him to the unknown world where the Stranger had based himself. Waking up in the Stranger's custody, Osha followed him as the man went out to take a swim and claimed his lightsaber, unaware that he was aware of her actions. Noticing how she thought killing an unarmed foe was not honorable, the Stranger managed to convince her into letting him live and divulged details of his past, attempting to tempt Osha into doubting the ideals of the Jedi and instead embrace his own. All the while, Sol discovered that Mae had swapped places with her sister and subdued her, leaving the orbit of Khofar and promising to save Osha from Mae's master once they had a chance to truly talk.<ref name="Teach / Corrupt" />

Just as Sol departed, a Jedi investigation team under Master Vernestra Rwoh arrived on Khofar, where they discovered the aftermath of the battle with the Stranger. Unaware of who had committed the massacre, Padawan [[Mog Adana]] suggested that Sol had fallen to the dark side.<ref name="Teach / Corrupt" /> With all parties converging on Brendok once Sol returned to the world where all his troubles had began, as Sol activated his tracking beacon for the Jedi to follow him and Osha experienced a Force vision of his death on the planet, Sol and the Stranger began a [[Duel on Brendok|final duel]], after which Mae rejected the ways of anger and instead wanted to see Sol brought to justice for his crime: striking down her mother and lying about his actions. However, the revelation that her master had killed her mother broke Osha, who Force choked the Jedi Master—thereby killing a Jedi without a weapon—and bled his lightsaber.<ref name="The Acolyte" />

[[File:MasterAndAcolyte-TheAcolyte.png|thumb|right|250px|Verosha Aniseya turned to the dark side and replaced her sister as the Stranger's new acolyte.]]
Osha accepted the station as the Stranger's acolyte, while Mae allowed her memory of her sister to be wiped so she could be handed over to the Jedi. As the Jedi party under Rwoh arrived too late to catch the Stranger, Rwoh blamed the murders of Kelnecca, Indara, and Torbin on Sol. Having sensed her former disciple's presence, however, she met with Mae and requested her aid in finding the Stranger. Meanwhile, Osha returned to the Stranger's island with him as his new acolyte,<ref name="The Acolyte" /> all while Plagueis continued to lurk on the planet.<ref name="Acolyte Companion" />
